steps.body: Filling an outline with smaller shapes means covering it completely: no gaps left uncovered and no pieces stacked on top of each other.
steps.narration: Filling an outline with smaller shapes means covering it completely: no gaps left uncovered and no pieces stacked on top of each other.

widget.prompt: Sort each attempt at filling an outline.

items.label: pieces cover every part, none overlap
items.feedback: Complete cover with no overlaps — this is a correct fill.

items.label: small gaps left between pieces
items.feedback: Gaps mean part of the outline is still uncovered.

items.label: pieces stacked on each other
items.feedback: Stacking covers the same part twice and leaves other parts bare.

items.label: different pieces, still covering exactly
items.feedback: A different set of pieces is fine as long as the cover is exact.

widget.missFeedback: Check for two things: any gap, and any overlap.
widget.successFeedback: Sorted — a correct fill covers everything exactly once.

predict.prompt: Can one outline be filled correctly in more than one way?
predict.reveal: Different combinations of pieces can each cover the same outline exactly — a square can take two triangles, or four small squares.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1s fill outline.
invariants: A shape's defining attributes must stay fixed while colour, size and orientation vary.
misconceptions: Treating colour, size or orientation as if it decided what a shape is.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same shape?

widget.prompt: You fill an outline with 4 pattern blocks. What must be true when you finish?

options.label: Cover it completely with no gaps or overlaps
options.feedback: Correct — the pieces must cover the whole outline exactly, leaving no space and never stacking.

options.label: Leave small gaps between pieces
options.feedback: Gaps mean part of the outline is not covered, so the shape is not truly filled.

options.label: Stack pieces on top of each other
options.feedback: Overlapping covers the same region twice and leaves other parts bare.

options.label: Use pieces of any size at random
options.feedback: Pieces must fit the outline exactly; random sizes will not close it without gaps.

widget.prompt: Tap the piece that would fill the last gap in a half-filled square outline.

hotspots.label: circle
hotspots.feedback: A round piece leaves gaps at the corners, so the fill is never exact.

hotspots.label: oversized square
hotspots.feedback: A piece larger than the gap would overlap what is already placed.

hotspots.label: no piece at all
hotspots.feedback: Leaving the gap empty means the outline is not filled.

widget.missFeedback: Look for the piece whose edges match the empty space exactly.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — the matching triangle closes the gap exactly, with no overlap.

widget.prompt: A square is cut along one diagonal, leaving a triangle. How many corners does a triangle have?

commonErrors.feedback: That counts a corner twice, or counts the original square's fourth corner that this triangle does not use; trace only this triangle's own three corners.
That misses one corner of the finished triangle; count all the way around the outside.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Look again at the shape's sides and corners, counting each one exactly once.

widget.prompt: Arranging six matching triangle pieces around one centre point makes what shape?

options.label: A hexagon
options.feedback: Correct — arranging six matching triangle pieces around one centre makes a hexagon because they meet at a single centre point.

options.label: A circle
options.feedback: Straight-sided pieces cannot join into a circle; every edge they contribute stays straight.

options.label: A cone
options.feedback: That is a solid, but joining flat pieces edge to edge keeps the result flat.

options.label: Nothing — shapes cannot be joined
options.feedback: Shapes combine readily; a new, larger shape is exactly what composing produces.
